key_insight: A Bayesian-optimization search paired with discrete biorthogonal wavelet analysis enables fast, robust laser-frequency auto-locking without relying on blind parameter scanning.
engineering_relevance: This improves field-ready stabilization for quantum communication, quantum computing, and precision-measurement systems operating under drift and environmental perturbations.
method: Use Bayesian optimization to leverage prior observations and rapidly locate the frequency reference.
Apply discrete biorthogonal wavelet transformation to detect transition signals and distinguish the correct reference by their characteristic frequency gaps and magnitudes.
Lock the laser with a lead zirconate titanate-current double-servo loop for final stabilization.
evidence_signal: The method reports about 5× faster reference search than conventional scanning, >99.5% identification accuracy under severe disturbances, and a narrowed linewidth of 20 kHz after locking.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable historical data and correct wavelet-based signal features, so deployment must account for changing noise conditions and calibration drift.
paper_title: Rapid and robust laser-frequency auto-locking using Bayesian-optimization and discrete-wavelet-transformation algorithms
